girls are at risk of substance abuse if they have low self-esteem and poor communication skills, and if they use drugs to cope with stress.

girls who use substances are more likely to have low levels of coping skills, high levels of depressive symptoms and low levels of self esteem, and that girls who do not use substances are more like to have higher levels of communication, problem solving and refusal skills, self-efficacy and peer use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adolescent girls who are more likely to use substances tend to be less able to solve problems, have less effective coping strategies, and have lower self esteem and self efficacy.

adolescent girls who have strong coping skills, who feel confident in their abilities to communicate with others, who have high self-esteem and a positive body image, who are less likely to experience stress, and who have good mood management skills are less likely to use substances than those who have low levels of these factors.
